prompt: What does a double solid yellow line mean?
bankAnswer: No passing is permitted in either direction

decisions.prompt: What does a double solid yellow line mean?

options.text: No passing is permitted only for slower traffic
options.consequence: You thought the double line only bound slower traffic and pulled out to pass the slow truck. A car came over the hill in the lane you pulled into and had to swerve onto the shoulder to miss you.

options.text: No passing is permitted in either direction
No passing is required unless the road is clear
options.consequence: The road looked clear, so you pulled out. You could not see past the hill. A car came over the hill in the lane you pulled into and had to swerve onto the shoulder to miss you.

options.text: No passing is needed on a one-way road
options.consequence: You thought the double line only mattered on a one-way road. This road is two-way, and you pulled out to pass. A car came over the hill in the lane you pulled into and had to swerve onto the shoulder to miss you.

successText: You waited. A car came over the hill in the lane you would have been in. Once the line was broken again, you passed with a clear view.
ruleText: A solid yellow center line on your side means no passing; double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction.

citation.source: FHWA Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, 11th Edition

verified: Read in the FHWA PDFs, Nov 2026: the sign "shall be installed on the left-hand side of the roadway at the beginning of no-passing zones"; passing "is prohibited for traffic traveling adjacent to the solid line".
